why: Acorn Towers parking lot is a guarded chop-shop yard. Owner decision 128 removes Wyatt Alken and retains the calm crew and ordinary cars.

open_questions: Walk into the Acorn Towers lot through the gates and sliding doors without the gig. Check the lot is reachable on foot and in a car and the runtime door policy opens what it must.
Stand in the parking bays. Check the twelve 6th Street gangers and eleven parked 6th Street cars are present at their spots and calm, not crouched, armed or hostile.
Find Wyatt Alken. Check he leans on the wall smoking at the talk spot instead of standing in a quest pose or hunting the player.
Cross the lot's security and restricted-area triggers. Check entering does not trip an alarm or turn the gang hostile with the security system hidden.
Open the booth and back rooms. Check the bootleg container, shard, car keys and Johnny's shoes are absent rather than left as orphaned quest props.
Look at the main access-point terminal by the gate. Check whether it opens the gate; if it does, the gate should stay as vanilla and the door policy should leave it alone.

communities.why: The lot's ambient 6th Street crew and their vehicles: eleven 6th Street cars in their bays plus twelve gangers on tablet, tool, welding, drug, graffiti, phone and card-table spots. Vanilla only ever reactivates this whole community after the gig; every entry's initial phase is default and every resolved spot is an idle workspot, so it is the calm, pre-gig look for a gang-held parking lot. Combat group kept first under population priority.

variant_toggles.why: The lot's security-system variant. The street-story open-world and bugfix phases hide it (show 0); only the combat gameplay phase shows it (show 1). A normal, open-for-business lot should not have the quest security system armed, so keep it hidden at boot.

proximity_wait.why: The lot gate on the normal way in: a DoorControllerPS device streamed with the venue's devices prefab, so the post-proximity re-issue fires as the player reaches the lot. A door, not a workspot.
